title: RSA-155 with CUDA-MPQS
statement: Reported complete factorization of RSA-155 with GPU-assisted self-initializing quadratic sieving.

target.description: The named 512-bit RSA-155 challenge modulus, already previously factored; selected July 14, 2026 run.

time.note: 689.74 GPU-hours for 64-GPU sieving plus 10.90 GPU-hours for the single-GPU solve; not CPU core-hours or elapsed time.

memory.note: No memory bound is established in this selected extraction.

wall_time.note: Reported sieve-start-to-factors elapsed time across two jobs, not the arithmetic sum of per-GPU work.

energy.note: 239.78 kWh sieving plus 2.48 kWh solving, from sampled GPU power; not whole-system energy.

success.description: The paper reports one completed RSA-155 computation. That observed outcome is not a general whole-run success probability, nor is a dependency-level frequency such a probability.

review.scope: Checked Section V-G's run outcome, cost accounting and device/host verification report; no independent rerun or factor-witness verification.

evidence.locator: PDF pp. 8–9, Section V-G (RSA-155); PDF p. 3, Section IV-B host residuals; PDF p. 7, Table III.
evidence.interpretation: Targeted primary-text transcription; no full-paper audit, global frontier certification or independent implementation run.

limitations: A selected computation record, not a claim of the largest general integer factorization or a break of current RSA key sizes.
GPU-hours are not directly comparable to CPU core-hours; board energy excludes unmeasured host/system energy.
Other moduli and hardware points in Table III are outside this selected run; no whole-paper benchmark inventory is claimed.

experiment.hardware: 64 NVIDIA H100 GPUs across 16 nodes for sieving, then one H100 for GF(2) solving; CPU setup, I/O and coordinator large-prime matching remain.
experiment.software: CUDA-MPQS v1.0.5 for this RSA-155 run; later profiled versions in the same paper are not substituted.
experiment.parameters: F=6e8; M=8,388,608; L=8e13; u8sat wide accumulator; batch=16; graph unroll=4; autotuning off; legacy matrix stage.
experiment.reported_outcome: Two 78-digit prime factors, with device and host product checks reported by the authors. Factor bytes were not extracted or independently checked by the Atlas.
